key_insight: Lightweight online learning can improve nonlinear conjugate gradient robustness while deterministic safeguards retain control over optimization steps.
engineering_relevance: The approach preserves low-storage optimization and is promising for PDE-constrained problems where function and gradient evaluations are expensive.
method: Use one online extreme learning machine to predict NCG coefficients during restart recovery or persistent stagnation.
Use a second model only after line-search failure to propose a bounded correction to the fallback step size.
Accept predictions only after deterministic safeguards pass; train on existing trajectory data without extra function or gradient evaluations.
evidence_signal: Tests on 480 CUTEst problems improved robustness across six NCG variants at broadly comparable evaluation costs; a conductivity-identification example illustrated potential cost and runtime reductions.
watch_item: Benefits beyond the tested problems remain uncertain, and implementations must preserve descent, scale, and out-of-distribution safeguards.
paper_title: Safeguarded Learning-Assisted Nonlinear Conjugate Gradient Methods
